items.title: Use of SAP008 Formula in PM Work Centre
items.author: A_Siva-07
items.text:
Introduction: 
 If a maintenance order shows zero planned labour cost, the first place we need to look is one small field on the Costing tab of the work center. In PM, that field usually holds SAP008. We know SAP008 should be maintained in the formula field of the costing tab in PM Work centre. But we have not aware how SAP008 is working. In this blog I tried to explain how SAP008 is working. 
 What is SAP008? 
 SAP008 is the standard formula key which tells how much internal labour to be charged for a maintenance order. 
 It takes the Work hours from the maintenance order operation and uses them as the activity quantity. SAP then multiplies the hours by the activity price for the work center's cost center and activity type, which is maintained in KP26: 
 Labour cost = Work hours × activity price 

 This formula is used in two places in maintenance order, 
 Planned cost: when the order is created or costed, the planned work gives the planned labour cost. For example, 8H × 50 = 400. (8H work and 50 is the price maintained for activity type in KP26 for 1H) 
 Actual cost: when technicians confirm the operation time in IW41, the confirmed work is calculated in the same way and the cost is posted to the order. 
 Conclusion: 
 Without SAP008, or another costing formula in work centre, the planned and actual cost cannot be calculated. The order then shows zero internal labour cost, or we will get error CK430, "Missing formula in work center."

items.title: Determining Output Tax (MWST) from the Sold-to Party instead of the Ship-to Party in SAP S/4HANA SD
items.author: ReethikaHarikrishnan
items.text:
Introduction 
 In this blog , I have covered a requirement that I received , where they wanted to determine MWST tax(In Sales Order) based on Sold-to party location instead of Ship-to party's. Which basically means "Tax depends on who buys it, not where the goods go". 
 How standard tax determination works 
 The standard MWST access ("Departure Country / Destination Country") uses the departure country (from the delivering plant), the destination country (from the ship-to party), and the tax classifications of the customer and the material. Condition records in VK11 point to the tax code for each combination, for example 15% taxable, 0% GCC or 0% export. 
 Design and configuration 
 1. New condition table (V/03) 
 We created a new condition table, "Tax based on Sold-to Party" , with these fields: Departure country (ALAND), Country (LAND1), Tax classification 1 of the customer (TAXK1) and Tax classification of the material (TAXM1). 

 Figure 1– Condition table "Tax based on Sold-to Party" and its fields 
 2. Feed the sold-to country into the access (enhancement) 
 The key structure looks like the standard table, but the country used for this access must be the sold-to party’s country, not the ship-to party’s. This needs a small enhancement, with the same logic in the sales order and in billing so both always determine the same tax. Common ways to do this: 
 Add a custom field for the sold-to country to the pricing header communication structure (KOMK) and fill it in the pricing user exits: USEREXIT_PRICING_PREPARE_TKOMK in MV45AFZZ (order) and the corresponding exit in RV60AFZZ (billing). 
 Map the table’s country field to that custom field in the access sequence ("Fields" level), so only this access uses the sold-to country and the other accesses stay standard. 
 3. Access sequence for MWST 
 We added the new table to the MWST access sequence as the first access , marked Exclusive , ahead of the standard accesses. If a sold-to record is found, it wins. If not, the standard accesses still apply as a fallback. 

 Figure 2 – MWST access sequence with the sold-to access first and exclusive 
 4. Condition records (VK11) 
 We maintained records for every relevant sold-to country and classification combination: domestic taxable (15%), GCC (0%), other export (0%, exempt). A spreadsheet covering all countries (about 170 records) made maintenance and review much easier. 

 Figure 4 – Selecting the new key combination in VK11 

 Figure 5 – Condition records maintained per sold-to country 
 5. Cut-over 
 The new logic applies only to new documents after transport to production. Existing open orders keep their already-determined tax only. 
 Conclusion 
 Determining tax by the sold-to party is a small configuration change with a big compliance impact. Technically it needs a new condition table, the sold-to country fed into that access through a small enhancement, and an exclusive first access in the MWST access sequence. The most important step is not technical: agree the tax treatment for every partner combination with your tax advisors first, then test each combination end to end. 
 Have you implemented any non-standard tax determination in SD? Please share your approach in the comments

items.title: Updating Equipment Partner Data in Bulk Using PM_PARTNER_UPDATE in SAP PM
items.author: LOURDES_16
items.text:
Introduction 
 In SAP Plant Maintenance, equipment master data is one of the important master data in maintenance. Along with equipment details, businesses may also need to maintain partner information such as Sold-to Party. When there are only a few equipment records, we can maintain or change the partner details manually through transaction IE02. But what happens when the business needs to update partner information for hundreds or thousands of equipment records? 
 Maintaining each equipment individually can take a lot of time. In such cases, a custom upload program can help us upload equipment details and their corresponding partner information in bulk. In this blog, let's look at how the function module PM_PARTNER_UPDATE can be used to update equipment partner information through a custom upload program. 
 Business Scenario 
 Consider a company that manages a large number of equipment across different customer locations. As part of a business requirement, the company needs to upload new equipment into SAP and assign the corresponding Sold-to Party to each equipment. The input file contains equipment details along with partner information. 
 For example: 

 Equipment 
 Description 
 Partner Function 
 Partner Number 

 10001 
 Pump 
 SP 
 100001 

 10001 
 Pump 
 SP 
 100002 

 10001 
 Pump 
 SP 
 100003 
 Instead of maintaining these partner details manually in IE02 for every equipment, we can develop a custom upload program to process the records. 
 Equipment master data can be created using the appropriate standard equipment creation. Once the equipment is created and its object number is available, we can use PM_PARTNER_UPDATE to maintain the corresponding partner assignments. The function module uses the IHPA table parameter to pass partner update information. Some of the important fields to use are: 
 OBJNR: Object number of the equipment. 
 PARVW: Partner function, such as SP 
 PARNR: Partner number to be assigned. 
 UPDKZ: Update indicator. 
 Why Is UPDKZ Important? 
 One important thing to remember while using PM_PARTNER_UPDATE is maintaining the correct value in the UPDKZ field. Just populating the equipment object number, partner function and partner number is not enough. The update indicator tells SAP what operation needs to be performed on the partner record. 
 The commonly encountered values are: 

 UPDKZ 
 Description 

 U 
 Update partner record 

 D 
 Mark a partner record for deletion 

 I 
 Insert new entry 
 This is an important step in the upload program. If the update indicator is not maintained correctly, the expected partner operation may not take place. After processing the upload records, it is important to verify whether the partner assignments have been updated correctly. We can use transaction IE03 to display the equipment and check the assigned partner details. We should also ensure that the upload program handles error messages, invalid partner numbers and unsuccessful updates properly. 
 Conclusion 
 When dealing with a large volume of equipment master data, a custom upload program can reduce manual effort and make the process easier. Using PM_PARTNER_UPDATE is one approach to handle equipment partner assignments in bulk. However, maintaining the correct UPDKZ value is an important part of this process. A small field like UPDKZ can make a significant difference in whether the partner record is inserted, updated or deleted.

items.text:
We are a U.S. manufacturing company running SAP ERP 6.0 EHP8 (SAP_APPL 618, SP-Level 0007) with SAP S/4HANA Finance 1605 and HU-managed inventory. 
 We are looking for the recommended SAP process for correcting a shipping shortage after PGI and billing have been completed. 
 Scenario: 
 • A customer ordered 24 pallets of finished goods. 
 • All 24 pallets were picked, PGI was posted and the invoice was transmitted to the customer. 
 • Due to a warehouse error, only one pallet was physically loaded onto the truck. The remaining 23 pallets are still in our warehouse. 
 • SAP shows all 24 pallets as shipped and invoiced. 
 Business and Financial Requirements: 
 Due to the customer's invoicing and payment process, we cannot cancel the original invoice and issue a replacement invoice. Once the original invoice is transmitted to the customer, it remains in their system. We do not have a mechanism to communicate that the original invoice has been canceled and replaced. 
 The customer will short-pay the original invoice for the goods they did not receive. Therefore, our accounting records must align with the customer's records for payment reconciliation, auditing and internal control purposes. 
 We need to accomplish the following: 
 • Maintain the original invoice without reversing or canceling it. 
 • Issue a separate credit memo for the 23 pallets that were not shipped, referencing the original invoice. 
 • Maintain both the original invoice and credit memo as separate open items in Accounts Receivable until the customer's payment and shortage deduction are reconciled. 
 • Restore the 23 pallets to unrestricted-use inventory, preferably maintaining their original HU numbers. 
 • Ensure the HUs are available for picking and shipping against future sales orders. 
 • Correct sales revenue, inventory valuation and the associated cost of goods sold. 
 • Maintain a clear audit trail and document flow linking the original invoice, credit memo and inventory correction. 
 Questions: 

 Would the standard SAP returns order process, referencing the original billing document, be the recommended solution even though the goods never physically left our warehouse? 

 Can the original HUs be restored to available inventory through a returns delivery without reversing the original invoice or creating duplicate HUs? 

 Are there any complications related to the original picking, packing or HU statuses that would prevent this process? 

 Which movement types and transaction codes would be appropriate for this scenario? 

 Is there another standard SAP process specifically designed to correct shipping shortages after PGI and billing without canceling the original invoice? 
 We would like to establish a standard, repeatable process for these situations that satisfies both our warehouse and financial requirements, rather than relying on unrelated manual inventory adjustments. 
 Any guidance on the recommended transaction flow, movement types and necessary configuration would be greatly appreciated. 
 Thank you!

 A new LGM user is created as part of the BTP user management. 
 This new user never logged into the LGM Web Interface 
 The new user does login into the Logistics APP (iOS or Android) and get's shown a selection dialog to choose his/her default warehouse -> The selection ends with an error -> the APP can't be used

7.summary: A product overview of SAP Joule Studio, an AI-first environment for building agents, workflows and applications from natural-language intent. It describes two access paths (Web UI for business users, CLI for professional developers) and a six-step intent-based process: Intent, Requirements (PRD), Specification, Solution, Testing, Deployment. It names four knowledge sources used during solution discovery (SAP LeanIX, SAP Knowledge Graph, SAP Domain Models, SAP Signavio). The text is descriptive and high-level; it gives no concrete CLI commands, config file format, artefact examples or code. The post is truncated mid-way through the CLI section.
key_points: Joule Studio offers two paths: a browser-based Web UI and a CLI for local IDE work, both following the same intent-based method.

The six steps are Intent, Requirements (PRD with personas, user stories, scope), Specification (architecture, API references, data models, task list), Solution, Testing in an isolated sandbox, and Deployment.
Specification step auto-discovers SAP APIs from the SAP Business Accelerator Hub.
Solution discovery consults SAP LeanIX (landscape), SAP Knowledge Graph (API discovery and fit-gap), SAP Domain Models (patterns and controls) and SAP Signavio (process insight).
Users reach Joule Studio from Joule Work by selecting Develop in the main navigation.
The post says the steps are non-linear and that teams can loop back after reviewing generated artefacts.
technical_details: Joule Studio Web UI (browser, conversational) and Joule Studio CLI (local IDE, config-file driven, per the post's wording).
Quick Create option skips clarifying questions and goes straight to solution generation.
Artefacts: PRD, implementation blueprint (spec), generated agents/automations/applications.
Knowledge sources: SAP LeanIX, SAP Knowledge Graph, SAP Domain Models, SAP Signavio.
SAP Business Accelerator Hub as the API catalogue source.
No version numbers, CLI syntax or file formats are given in the text shown.
7.why_it_matters: It gives an accurate map of how Joule Studio's intent-to-deployment pipeline is organised, which is useful for deciding where human review fits. As a source it is mostly marketing-level and does not let a developer reproduce anything.
7.teaching_angle: Use it as a 'what is Joule Studio' orientation slide, then ask trainees to map each of the six steps to an artefact they could review (PRD, spec, sandbox test) and to a traditional ABAP/RAP equivalent (requirements doc, design, transport, test, release). Point out that the post gives no CLI examples, so hands-on claims need checking in the product docs.

30.summary: A developer reports that saving a modified global ABAP class via ADT (Eclipse) fails with 'Save failure: SAP code was changed outside of modification brackets!' (message SEDI_ADT016). They added a parameter to a public method in a Z class in one system, while the same kind of change worked on other classes. They suspect a 'protected section' that appears in ADT just before PRIVATE SECTION, which was not in the original system, and are unsure whether the modification assistant was switched off. The post is a question with no answer or resolution in the text.
key_points: The save is a PUT to /sap/bc/adt/oo/classes/<class>/source/main with lockHandle and corrNr parameters.
The backend returns exception ExceptionResourceSaveFailure with T100 key SEDI_ADT / 016.
The author is unsure whether the modification assistant is on or off.
The author suspects an extra empty 'PROTECTED SECTION' visible in ADT, absent from the original system.
No answer or fix is in the post; the author asks what the problem is and how to solve it.
The same kind of change succeeded on other global classes, so the issue looks object-specific or system-specific.
technical_details: Error text: 'Save failure: SAP code was changed outside of modification brackets!' (SEDI_ADT 016).
Request: PUT /sap/bc/adt/oo/classes/zmyclassname/source/main?lockHandle=...&corrNr=...
Response property corrNr='*'.
Environment as reported: Eclipse 2026-09, ADT 3.62.0, backend 7.58 SP 1.
Relevant concepts to check: modification assistant setting in ADT, SE95 modifications, and any enhancement or modification touching the class source.
The post is titled as a Z class but the error refers to 'SAP code', so the object's modification status is worth verifying.
30.why_it_matters: ADT saves are rejected when the server sees source changes outside modification brackets, which blocks routine repairs in systems where the class source has drifted. Diagnosing this means comparing the target system's source with the original and checking modification and enhancement state, not just retrying the save.
30.developer_problem: An ADT save of a modified global class fails with SEDI_ADT016 'SAP code was changed outside of modification brackets', and the developer does not know whether the cause is the modification assistant setting or an extra section in the class source.
30.teaching_angle: Good interview or lab case on the difference between modification assistant, modifications (SE95) and enhancements, and on reading ADT communication logs. Ask trainees to list checks: compare source with the original version, look for a pre-existing modification in the target, confirm the modification assistant setting, and check whether a protected section was introduced by an earlier change. Note that the post does not confirm a cause.

38.summary: An incident write-up on an IoT setup that stopped reaching SAP BTP on October 15, 2026, when DigiCert Global Root G5 replaced older roots (SAP Note 3566727). It has two layers: Arduino sketches with hard-coded, outdated PEM root certificates, which were fixed by reflashing, and a five-year-old Node.js app on the legacy cflinuxfs3 stack that was never restaged, so its droplet kept old runtime and certificate trust. After migrating to cflinuxfs5 and the latest Node.js, the author used the AI chat in SAP Build Code to fix compatibility and npm dependency problems. The end of the post (takeaways) is cut off.
key_points: The error on the app side was 'Cannot connect to the bound SAP HANA Cloud database', while HANA Cloud was healthy.
Cloud Foundry reuses the existing droplet until the app is restaged or redeployed, so stack and runtime stay frozen.
Node.js uses its own bundled CA list unless specific flags are set, so an old runtime cannot trust a new root.
Arduino root certificates are hard-coded in the sketch and need a firmware update.
The migration to cflinuxfs5 and latest Node.js needed fixes for Node.js spec changes and npm dependencies, helped by SAP Build Code AI chat.
The author's main lesson is that 'stable operation' is not the same as 'maintenance-free'.
technical_details: SAP Note 3566727; DigiCert Global Root G5 migration in BTP Cloud Foundry; event date October 15, 2026.
Stacks: cflinuxfs3 (Ubuntu 18.04, retired), cflinuxfs4 (Ubuntu 22.04), cflinuxfs5 (Ubuntu 24.04).
Commands: cf restage or cf redeploy to rebuild the droplet on a new stack.
Buildpack: Node.js buildpack; HANA Cloud bound through service binding.
Arduino: root cert as PEM string loaded into the HTTPS client library.
Tooling: AI chat feature in SAP Build Code.
Note: the post does not name the Node.js flag for system CA use; if you need that, check Node.js and BTP docs.
38.why_it_matters: It shows why certificate rotations on BTP can break things that look unrelated, and it gives a clear checklist: check the app's stack, check restage history, and check the runtime's trust store. For anyone running BTP workloads, the cflinuxfs3 retirement and the droplet behaviour are concrete operational risks.
38.teaching_angle: Good ops-and-troubleshooting case study for BTP courses. Ask trainees to explain why a healthy HANA Cloud can still give a connection error, what cf restage changes, and how a Node.js runtime decides which CAs to trust. Pair it with a lab that lists stack and buildpack versions with cf app and cf stacks.

39.summary: A short blog intro about making Mileage facet visibility in an SAP Travel Expense application depend on the selected travel mode (shown only for Car). The author says the standard app controls facet visibility through a virtual element in the RAP consumption layer, and that they used an implicit enhancement to add the condition. The text ends before any code, virtual element name, enhancement point or test is shown, so the actual technique cannot be checked from this post.
key_points: Requirement: show the Mileage section only when the travel mode is Car; hide it for Train, Flight or Bus.
The author first considered UI configuration, then found the standard uses a virtual element in the RAP consumption layer.
The approach is an implicit enhancement that extends the standard logic without changing the UI configuration.
The post does not name the virtual element, the class, the enhancement or the annotations used.
The full body of the article is missing from the text provided.
technical_details: Context: SAP Travel Expense application built on SAP RAP, consumption layer (projection) with a virtual element.
Mechanism named: implicit enhancement.
Target: facet visibility of the Mileage section.
No code, annotation or enhancement-spot names are given in the text shown.
In CDS, virtual elements are usually declared with @ObjectModel.virtualElement and @ObjectModel.virtualElementCalculatedBy; the post does not confirm that this is what the standard uses.
39.why_it_matters: Working out how standard SAP apps decide UI visibility through RAP virtual elements is useful for anyone extending SAP-delivered Fiori apps without touching UI configuration. The idea is sound, but the post as given does not show enough to repeat it.
39.developer_problem: Show or hide a standard Travel Expense facet (Mileage) based on the selected travel mode without changing the standard UI configuration.
39.teaching_angle: Use it as a discussion prompt on extensibility: where to hook a condition when the standard uses a virtual element, and how an implicit enhancement differs from an explicit enhancement point. Ask trainees what they would check first, such as the consumption view, the virtual element calculation class, and the facet annotations. Do not rely on this post for code.

42.summary: A tutorial on unit-testing an AUTHORITY-CHECK inside the GET_GLOBAL_AUTHORIZATIONS method of a RAP behaviour implementation, using a custom authorization object Z_RAUTH_D1 with field ACTVT. It shows global authorization in the behaviour definition, the handler logic that sets %create/%update/%delete to allowed or unauthorized, and a local ABAP Unit test class that declares FRIENDS, uses CREATE OBJECT and calls the handler method. The test code is partly shown and truncated, and the post does not explain how the user's authorizations are set up for the test run. The test assertions are weak in parts.
key_points: Global authorization is enabled in the behaviour definition with 'authorization master ( global )'.
GET_GLOBAL_AUTHORIZATIONS checks requested_authorizations-%create / %update / %delete and sets result with if_abap_behv=>auth-allowed / auth-unauthorized.
The handler uses AUTHORITY-CHECK OBJECT 'Z_RAUTH_D1' ID 'ACTVT' FIELD '01' / '02' / '06' (create, update, delete).
The test class uses FOR TESTING, DURATION SHORT, RISK LEVEL HARMLESS, a FRIENDS relation to the handler, and a SETUP that creates the object.
The '00' (off) case asserts only assert_not_initial, not that the result is unauthorized, so the negative path is not really tested.
The author does not address that AUTHORITY-CHECK results depend on the running user's roles, so the test can pass or fail by environment.
technical_details: BDEF: authorization master ( global ).
Method: GET_GLOBAL_AUTHORIZATIONS, with requested_authorizations and result structures for the RAP global authorization type.
Constants: if_abap_behv=>mk-on (request flag) and if_abap_behv=>auth-allowed / auth-unauthorized (result).

Test framework: ABAP Unit (FOR TESTING, CL_ABAP_UNIT_ASSERT with assert_equals and assert_not_initial), CDS test double framework (IF_CDS_TEST_ENVIRONMENT, IF_OSQL_TEST_ENVIRONMENT, CL_ABAP_BEHV_TEST_ENVIRONMENT).
Coverage: ABAP Coverage tool in ADT (described, not shown).
Code gaps: class_setup and the environment creation are not shown; some variables are commented out.
42.why_it_matters: Authorization logic in RAP is easy to get wrong and hard to test, and the post addresses a real gap. However, the chosen design leaves the authority check tied to the test user's roles, and the negative case is weakly asserted, so the test gives less confidence than it looks.
42.developer_problem: How to unit-test an AUTHORITY-CHECK in a RAP global authorization method so that each activity (01, 02, 06) is verified to be allowed or refused.
42.teaching_angle: Strong exercise for a RAP course. Ask trainees to make the negative case assert '%create = if_abap_behv=>auth-unauthorized' and to explain how to control the authority outcome (test user with specific roles, or refactoring the check into a call that can be substituted in tests). Discuss why unit tests that rely on sy-subrc from AUTHORITY-CHECK are environment-dependent.

47.summary: A product-management article on promoting Joule Studio agents across three tenants (Development, Test, Production) using Git-based workflows. It describes separate tenants with Joule Work, Joule Studio and SAP Cloud Identity Services, and walks through a GitHub example: create the agent by intent, deploy to the sandbox, connect and push the solution to Git, then copy the generated deploy.yml into a Test-specific workflow with tenant-specific secrets. The post is concrete about naming and steps and ends before the release and approval flow for Production.
key_points: Three tenants (Development, Test, Production), each with Joule Work, Joule Studio and SAP Cloud Identity Services.
Git repo receives the solution; deployment workflow files are generated automatically on push.
For Test, copy .github/workflows/deploy.yml to deploy-to-test.yml, rename the workflow, and swap in TEST_-prefixed variables and secrets.
Each tenant needs its own SCI application and environment-specific GitHub organisation secrets.
Promotion to Production requires a Joule Studio release with an approval process (the details are cut off in the text).
GitHub is the example provider; the post says other providers follow the same principles.
technical_details: Secrets/variables named: TEST_SCI_TENANT_URL, TEST_SCI_CLIENT_ID, TEST_SCI_CLIENT_SECRET, TEST_JOULE_STUDIO_URL (generic names SCI_TENANT_URL, SCI_CLIENT_ID, SCI_CLIENT_SECRET, JOULE_STUDIO_URL).
Files: .github/workflows/deploy.yml (generated sample) and deploy-to-test.yml (copy).
Workflow name changed from 'Deploy to Joule Studio' to 'Deploy to Joule Studio Test Tenant'.
Actions tab in GitHub used to trigger and monitor deployments.
Components: SAP Cloud Identity Services application per tenant, GitHub organisation-level secrets.
Joule Studio release object used for Production promotion (details not in the text shown).
47.why_it_matters: It gives a practical pattern for CI/CD of Joule Studio agents, with environment isolation by tenant and credentials. Teams that are used to transport-based landscape promotion in ABAP will find the mapping to Git, release and approval useful.
47.teaching_angle: Use it in a DevOps or BTP module to compare tenant-based promotion with CTS transports. Ask trainees to write the Production workflow variant, to say where approvals sit, and to list which secrets must never be shared across tenants. Note that the post has no YAML sample and the Production step is truncated.

65.summary: A consultant on S/4HANA 2025 asks whether API_PURCHASEORDER_2 can create purchase orders with header-level pricing conditions that SAP distributes to line items. The post says the API only handles item-level conditions and asks three things: a standard header-condition API, whether header and item levels are both supported, and any alternative OData or enhancement route. No answer is included in the text.
key_points: Business need: enter conditions at PO header level and let standard condition distribution spread them across items.

44.summary: A Japanese blog describes an IoT incident where an Arduino-based sensor system stopped reaching SAP BTP Cloud Foundry on 15 October 2026, when the DigiCert Global Root G5 transition (SAP Note 3566727) took effect. The root cause was an old root certificate hard-coded in the Arduino sketch, followed by a second failure: a Node.js app on cflinuxfs3 could not reach SAP HANA Cloud because its restaged-never runtime and bundled CA store did not trust G5. The author fixed it by moving to cflinuxfs5 and a newer Node.js runtime, using SAP Build Code's AI chat to resolve dependency issues.
key_points: The Arduino device stopped communicating because its PEM root certificate was hard-coded in the sketch, so it could not be updated automatically.
The CF app kept running on the old cflinuxfs3 stack and old Node.js runtime. Cloud Foundry keeps the existing droplet until the app is restaged or redeployed.
Node.js uses its own bundled CA list unless told to use the OS store, so the old runtime did not trust DigiCert G5. This caused the HANA Cloud TLS errors.
The fix was to move to cflinuxfs5 (Ubuntu 24.04) and a newer Node.js version. The author reports Node.js breaking changes and npm dependency errors, which were resolved with SAP Build Code's AI chat.

The post's recommendations: plan certificate rotation for edge devices (OTA updates or hardware replacement), check the BTP Cockpit for stack migration warnings, and restage or update buildpacks regularly.
technical_details: SAP Note 3566727: root certificate replacement on SAP BTP Cloud Foundry, moving to DigiCert Global Root G5; cutover date 15 Oct 2026 per the post.
Arduino (Wi-Fi module) PEM root certificate embedded as a string in the sketch and loaded by the HTTPS client library.
Cloud Foundry stacks named in the post: cflinuxfs3 (Ubuntu 18.04, deprecated/removed), cflinuxfs4 (Ubuntu 22.04), cflinuxfs5 (Ubuntu 24.04).
Node.js (Node.js buildpack) uses its bundled CA store by default; the OS store is used only with a specific option.
Failing connection: Node.js app to SAP HANA Cloud over TLS.
Remediation: cf restage or redeploy on cflinuxfs5 with a newer Node.js buildpack. Tool used: SAP Build Code AI chat (the author's own experience).

Proposed format: 6 characters from the confirmation date (ddmmyy) plus last 4 digits of the sales order customer number
The example string 2810262341 is 10 characters, which matches the standard batch number length (CHARG, 10 characters)
The post does not say which SAP mechanism it would hook into or which release is in use
Uniqueness is not addressed: two orders for the same customer on the same day would produce the same batch number for the same material
technical_details: Batch field: CHARG (10 characters in the standard batch number, MCH1/MCHA tables)
Confirmation: production order confirmation (CO11N/CO15 or the related BAPI) does not itself create the batch; batches are normally assigned at goods receipt for the production order

Customer number is not on the production order by default; it would have to be derived from the sales order linked to the order (for example via the sales order/MTO link), which the post does not explain

Possible routes to verify in the target release (not stated in the post): batch number assignment customizing with a custom number-range or determination logic, and batch-related BAdIs or user exits called at batch creation. Check exact names in your release before using them
90.why_it_matters: Batch number design is a real requirement in process manufacturing and make-to-order. The post is useful as a requirement, but it is shallow: it lacks the hook point, the uniqueness rule, and the fact that the batch is usually created at goods receipt rather than at confirmation.
90.developer_problem: How can a batch number be generated automatically with custom logic (date plus customer digits) when a production order is confirmed?
90.teaching_angle: Good exercise on the difference between confirmation and goods receipt in PP, on where batch numbers are assigned, and on designing unique batch keys. Ask learners to identify the hook point in their release and to explain why a date plus partial customer number needs a uniqueness check or a number-range fallback.

Consequence: no adaptation session can start, so no adaptation actions are available on the standard app
Environment: SAP Business Application Studio (BAS) with the Adaptation Editor

technical_details: Tool: SAP Adaptation Editor in SAP Business Application Studio (SAP Fiori tools)

95.developer_problem: Why are the UI Adaptation and Navigation modes disabled in the Adaptation Editor in SAP BAS, and how can an adaptation be started?

digest.headline: Thin day for core ABAP: a RAP authority-check unit test, an ADT save error, an EML dump, and a BTP certificate outage lesson.
digest.overview:
Today's core ABAP material is mostly developer questions without answers. They cover an ADT save failure (SEDI_ADT016), a BEHAVIOR_ILLEGAL_STATEMENT dump when calling I_WBSBillOfMaterialTP via EML, and a missing change log from BAPI_PRICES_CONDITIONS. The one tutorial with code tests AUTHORITY-CHECK in a RAP GET_GLOBAL_AUTHORIZATIONS method with ABAP Unit, but its negative case is weakly asserted. The Joule Studio posts are product descriptions with little a developer can reproduce.

The most useful operational item is the BTP certificate incident (SAP Note 3566727, DigiCert Global Root G5). It was posted in English and in Japanese. A Cloud Foundry app on the old cflinuxfs3 stack kept its old droplet and runtime, and lost its HANA Cloud connection. For ABAP trainers, the practical value is in the RAP and ADT troubleshooting cases, each of which needs verification because no answers were given.

top_stories.title: Unit-testing AUTHORITY-CHECK in RAP global authorization
top_stories.summary: A tutorial tests GET_GLOBAL_AUTHORIZATIONS with a custom object Z_RAUTH_D1 (ACTVT 01/02/06), using 'authorization master ( global )' in the BDEF and a local ABAP Unit class with a FRIENDS relation. The handler sets %create/%update/%delete to auth-allowed or auth-unauthorized. The '00' case only asserts assert_not_initial, so the negative path is not really verified. The results also depend on the test user's roles.
top_stories.why_it_matters: Authorization in RAP is hard to test. A test that depends on the running user's roles and does not assert the unauthorized result gives false confidence.

top_stories.title: ADT save fails with SEDI_ADT016 'SAP code was changed outside of modification brackets'
top_stories.summary: Saving a changed public method signature in a global class fails in ADT 3.62.0 against backend 7.58 SP1. The author is unsure whether the modification assistant is active and suspects a new empty PROTECTED SECTION. The same change worked on other classes. No answer was given.
top_stories.why_it_matters: It blocks routine class changes. The diagnosis is to compare the source with the original, and to check modification (SE95) and the assistant setting. The cause is unconfirmed.

top_stories.title: BTP root certificate migration (Note 3566727) broke an IoT system in two layers
top_stories.summary: On 15 Oct 2026 the DigiCert Global Root G5 change stopped an Arduino device (hard-coded PEM root) and a Node.js app on cflinuxfs3. Cloud Foundry keeps the droplet until restage or redeploy, and Node.js uses its own bundled CA list. The fix was to move to cflinuxfs5 and a current Node.js, with help from SAP Build Code AI chat. A Japanese version of the same post is included.
top_stories.why_it_matters: A healthy HANA Cloud can still return connection errors when the app's runtime is old. Check stack, restage history and the runtime's trust store.

top_stories.title: EML call to I_WBSBillOfMaterialTP dumps with BEHAVIOR_ILLEGAL_STATEMENT
top_stories.summary: The dump occurs in SAPLCMFE (CO-PC-PCP) because MESSAGE E ran while the BO implementation for R_WBSBILLOFMATERIALTP was active. The dump says the real error may sit at a higher call level. No EML code was posted.
top_stories.why_it_matters: The dump hides the real cause. Read the call stack to find the actual error, and note that classic MESSAGE E is illegal in RAP implementation phases.

top_stories.title: Standard Travel Expense facet visibility via virtual element and implicit enhancement
top_stories.summary: The author says the standard app controls the Mileage facet through a RAP consumption-layer virtual element and that an implicit enhancement adds a travel-mode condition. The text ends before any code.
top_stories.why_it_matters: The idea of extending a standard app without touching UI configuration is useful, but it can't be reproduced from this text.

top_stories.title: Joule Studio: pipeline overview and Git-based promotion across three tenants
top_stories.summary: One post describes the six-step intent-to-deployment flow, a Web UI and a CLI. Another shows promotion across Dev/Test/Prod tenants. It copies the generated .github/workflows/deploy.yml to deploy-to-test.yml with TEST_ prefixed secrets, and each tenant gets its own SCI application. The Production release and approval step is cut off.
top_stories.why_it_matters: The Git workflow is the concrete part. It maps to CTS landscape promotion, but the posts show no CLI syntax.

top_stories.title: Claude tool-calling over SAP Commerce OCC through a BFF
top_stories.summary: A prototype exposes OCC coupon APIs as Claude tools. The Angular chat calls a BFF, which runs a two-turn loop. Turn one uses tools and turn two does not. The example performs write operations.
top_stories.why_it_matters: It raises real governance questions: no visible authorization check on which customer the agent may modify, no per-tool error handling, and one tool round only.

deep_dives.title: Testing global authorization in RAP with ABAP Unit
deep_dives.explanation:
The BDEF declares `authorization master ( global )`. The behavior pool's `GET_GLOBAL_AUTHORIZATIONS` method receives `requested_authorizations` and fills `result`. For each requested flag (`%create`, `%update`, `%delete` equal to `if_abap_behv=>mk-on`), the handler runs `AUTHORITY-CHECK OBJECT 'Z_RAUTH_D1' ID 'ACTVT' FIELD '01'`, `'02'` or `'06'`. It sets the result to `if_abap_behv=>auth-allowed` or `auth-unauthorized` based on `sy-subrc`.

The test class is local, `FOR TESTING`, with `DURATION SHORT` and `RISK LEVEL HARMLESS`. It declares a FRIENDS relation to the handler class so it can create the object and call the method. The article's weak point is the negative case. It asserts only `assert_not_initial`, which passes whether the result is allowed or unauthorized. A real test asserts `%create = if_abap_behv=>auth-unauthorized`.

The second problem is that `AUTHORITY-CHECK` reads the running user's authorizations, so the test result depends on the system and user. Options: run with a test user whose roles are known, or move the check into a small class behind an interface that a test double can replace. The article's text does not cover this.

The post mentions ABAP Coverage in ADT and the test doubles (CDS, OSQL, behavior test environment), but the shown code doesn't set up an environment.

deep_dives.title: BEHAVIOR_ILLEGAL_STATEMENT in EML calls: reading the dump
deep_dives.explanation:
The dump arises in program `SAPLCMFE` when `MESSAGE E` runs while the BO implementation of `R_WBSBILLOFMATERIALTP` is active. RAP restricts statements that interrupt processing, such as classic error messages, during behavior implementation phases. The dump itself warns that the true error may be at a higher call level.

RAP convention is to return messages through the `reported` and `failed` structures. Our post doesn't show the EML code, so this guidance is general RAP practice, not a confirmed fix for this case.

Method: open the dump's call stack in ST22 or ADT, and find the first frame outside the SAP-internal code. Then check which input made the legacy code raise an error (a missing mandatory field, wrong entity key, or an invalid sequence). Write the `MODIFY ENTITIES OF I_WBSBillOfMaterialTP` call with `FAILED` and `REPORTED` captured, followed by `COMMIT ENTITIES`, and read the results before assuming a platform bug.

deep_dives.title: ADT save error SEDI_ADT016: what to check
deep_dives.explanation:
The save is a PUT to `/sap/bc/adt/oo/classes/<class>/source/main` with `lockHandle` and `corrNr`. The backend answers `ExceptionResourceSaveFailure`, T100 message `SEDI_ADT 016`: 'SAP code was changed outside of modification brackets'. The report is from ADT 3.62.0 against 7.58 SP1, and no cause was confirmed.

The message implies the server treats the class as SAP-delivered code with modification handling. Checks: is the object really a Z class or does it contain SAP code, is the modification assistant active for it, does SE95 show existing modifications, and has an earlier change introduced an empty `PROTECTED SECTION`? Compare the current source with the original version.

Use the ADT communication log to see the actual request and response. These are diagnostic steps to try, not a confirmed fix.

post_drafts.title: Your RAP authority test may prove nothing
post_drafts.text:
*Testing AUTHORITY-CHECK in RAP?* Watch the assertions.

A tutorial tests GET_GLOBAL_AUTHORIZATIONS (authorization master ( global )) with ABAP Unit.

Two problems:
- The '00' case asserts only assert_not_initial. It passes even if the result is allowed.
- AUTHORITY-CHECK uses the test user's roles, so results change by system.

*Better:* assert %create = if_abap_behv=>auth-unauthorized, and put the check behind an interface you can substitute in tests.

post_drafts.text:
*BTP certificate change (Note 3566727)* broke a 5-year-old setup.

The Node.js app showed 'Cannot connect to bound SAP HANA Cloud database'. HANA was fine.

Cause: Cloud Foundry keeps the droplet until you restage. The app sat on cflinuxfs3 with an old Node.js and old CA list.

- when was it last restaged?
- does the runtime trust the new root?

post_drafts.text:

A developer calling I_WBSBillOfMaterialTP via EML got a MESSAGE E inside an active BO implementation phase.

The dump itself says the real error may be higher in the call stack.

interview_questions.question: You unit-test a RAP GET_GLOBAL_AUTHORIZATIONS method that uses AUTHORITY-CHECK. What makes the test unreliable and how do you fix it?
interview_questions.answer: AUTHORITY-CHECK reads the authorizations of the user running the test, so the outcome depends on roles in that system. A test that passes in a developer system may fail in QA. Weak assertions make it worse, for example assert_not_initial on the result does not distinguish auth-allowed from auth-unauthorized. Assert the exact value, such as %create = if_abap_behv=>auth-unauthorized. To control the outcome, either run with a test user whose roles are known, or move the check behind an interface that a test double can replace. Then test each activity (01, 02, 06) in both allowed and refused states.

interview_questions.question: An EML call to a released BO ends in BEHAVIOR_ILLEGAL_STATEMENT with MESSAGE E in a standard program. How do you approach it?
interview_questions.answer: The dump says a MESSAGE E ran while a BO implementation was active, which RAP does not allow. The dump also warns the real error may be at a higher call level. I open the call stack and find the first frame outside the SAP internals, then check what input made the legacy code raise an error: missing mandatory fields, wrong keys or an invalid sequence. I make the EML call with FAILED and REPORTED captured and check them before COMMIT ENTITIES. I would not treat the dump line as the cause. If the input is valid and the dump persists, it goes to SAP as a product issue with the stack.

interview_questions.question: Saving a global class in ADT gives SEDI_ADT016 'SAP code was changed outside of modification brackets'. What do you check?
interview_questions.answer: The message means the backend treats the source as SAP code under modification control. First I confirm whether the object is really customer code or contains SAP-delivered parts. Then I check the modification assistant setting and SE95 for existing modifications on the object. I compare the current source with the original version, looking for unexpected changes such as a new empty PROTECTED SECTION. I also look at the ADT communication log for the PUT to /sap/bc/adt/oo/classes/.../source/main. The source post gives no confirmed cause, so these are diagnostic steps.
